_about: The Models tab of the hangar page (tools/hangar.html): every render Ryan judges, by chassis. A round adds its pictures under docs/hangar/renders/<chassis>/, moves the previous 'images' to 'before' with a summary, and writes 'when' and 'note'; then the page is republished with the new files (tools/hangar_data.py prints the files map). 'classes' is the silhouette classes section, a list of blocks shown in order.

classes.title: Silhouette classes
classes.plate: What a swapped component wears at a gun mount · the rule settled 30 September

blocks.note: Hardpoints are gun mounts. A weapon, or equipment that can look like one (a shield projector, a buff coil), wears its class at the next mount in the die's order, in its own maker's metal; armour panels and vents take a die entry and no mount, since they are applied to the whole machine. Five classes: barrel, twin barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, punching forward) and dish. A machine with more hardpoints than stock guns carries bare mount pads. Shown: a Minerva barrel, a Wainwright & Sutler rack, a Kestrel dish, an Arsenal blade.

Four refits rendered with RIFTGATE_FIT: the Honey Badger with a W&S Lance on the wrist, a Heat Sink (which shows nowhere), an Arsenal Blazethrower on the left pauldron and a Kestrel Deflector's dish on the right; the Clydesdale with an Arc Projector in place of the Lance and, on its bare mounts, a Missile Rack, Soulcutter Talons and an Overcharge Coil; the Kite with Soulcutter Talons as a wing blade and Meteor Artillery on the other tip; the Wild Boar with a Plasma Carbine and a Blazethrower on its rear quarters.

Ryan, 2 November: “Can't we just model different shapes as options, as needed?” A variant is a class in another form, modelled for the mounts its standard shape does not fit and named for its form, so any hardpoint may take it; a hardpoint declares, for each class, the variant it wears and its scale there, and every other hardpoint wears the class itself at its own scale. The first is the round launcher, for a round port or a pod's nose (the Polar Bear's ports, the Buzzard's pods), its face the square rack's missile tile one tube at a time. Shown in Minerva's and Wainwright & Sutler's metal; Classes on the Models tab shows it alone.

A second variant, of the barrel: the standard gun's barrel and muzzle alone, starting at the socket, for a mount whose receiver is inside the hull behind a port's wall (the Kite's inset mount, Ryan, 12 November: "the actual mount block is hidden", then "let it poke out more"). Shown in Kestrel's metal; the Kite's pictures show it worn.

badger.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its stock is the Rivet Gun alone, on the deck's ring as its class, the gimbals bare (the Canopy and the Coolant Jacket show nowhere); the missile box and the gimbals' autoguns went with the old stock.

clydesdale.when: Its batteries, their wells and its idle acts, 11 and 12 November.
clydesdale.note: Ryan, 11 November: “It has two dice, each with 5 sides ... if we put all 8 hardpoints back on its back, flipping dice would cause 4 to retreat into its hull ... and the other 4 to emerge ... the 4 pivoting vertical, then retreating downward vertically”; the checkerboard his pick. Eight square ports on the deck in two alternating batteries (Ryan: “Sure, square ports, and either trapdoors or split middle - slide open, both could work. Depends on geometry”), each a stripe frame round a real well with two trapdoors across it (12 November: “Should it be a hole?”), its gun on a drum that lifts, turns and pivots; the first battery up at rest (the Maxigun, the Twin Autoguns and the Enfilade Beam, the Shoring Jack's mount bare), the second (the Ankle Mortar, the Howitzer, the Airburst Shell, the Incendiary Shells) up while it carries Changed Over. The Changeover pivots the battery up upright and sinks it as the other's trapdoors drop open and its guns rise; the sunk battery's trapdoors swing shut and the risen guns pivot down, in 1.4 s (RIFTGATE_SEAL_DEBUG=1 turns it constantly, to judge running). Every stock gun its class at 0.62, the hull 3 deeper to stow a battery upright, the bed's boards lower, the stack behind the bed; the turrets, the lance, the gimbals and the cheek mounts gone. Its idle acts since that evening (Ryan: "Those all sound good. Don't need the old ones"): the battery on deck ranging where the head looks, a broadside drill (12 November: gun by gun was “a little dull”), a paw of the fore-right hoof, a breath down onto its hydraulics with the heat sink (a radiator now, dark fins over a core) glowing on the exhale, and the stowed hatches checked in a wave down the deck (his “like a do the wave effect”); Changed Over plays the second battery's own.

kite.when: The third mount and the intake, 12 November.
kite.note: Ryan, 12 November: a third mount "in front of the canopy, but inset, like the polar bear - so some of the barrel pokes out through a cut channel. Doesn't retract or anything"; "sink it horizontally into the hull more, so the actual mount block is hidden, and don't cut a channel all the way down the nose"; "Raise the gun's line a little"; "let it poke out more and cut the trough a little deeper vertically so the barrel isn't covered"; "a round rack would be warranted when a missile is slotted there". A port at the canopy's nose and a trough cut into the spine ahead of it, bare on the stock machine; a gun there is the port gun, its barrel alone out of the port, and a launcher the round rack against the port's wall (the third and fourth pictures: a Laser Carbine, a Shotfire Rack). The tail segment's flat face behind the canopy is an air intake ("Can the flat face behind the canopy also get an intake treatment?"). First cuts; how a dish, a blade or twin barrels sit in the port is a guess.

polar_bear.note: Ryan, 11 November: “There's no reason to keep hand build guns anywhere”: every stock gun wears its class, as a fitted one does, in its pin's fit, and what it sat in or on stays the chassis's. Then, of the ports: “Can't the polar bears guns start deeper? Why do they have to come all the way out? Like a round missile rack doesn't need to poke out at all”: each class sits at its depth in the ports' fits, a gun about as far out as the old hand-built ones and a round rack's face just inside the rim, and the seal sinks them 17.5 along their lines. The swapped studies are 11 November's too: four Shotfire Racks, and a Twin Autoguns, a Shotfire Rack, a Halo Projector and a Slugthrower.

skua.note: Ryan, 12 November: "Can we turn the skua's spine pods into intakes? And remove the pod burst animation." The two spine pods are air intakes, a dark mouth in a steel lip, and the burst is gone with the Flechette Pod's lock; the Pod is an ordinary gun in its stock now, a rack under the belly. A first cut.

needletail.when: Ryan's design of its two modes, 12 November.
needletail.note: Ryan, 12 November, his design: “In hover mode, two sets of vertical boosters on swivels. Front boosters are smaller, on the ends of short canards. Rear boosters are larger, and sit at the tip of horizontal tailfins. Four other tailfins are arranged in an X pattern. No apparent main wings. When changed into flight mode, all four boosters rotate to horizontal and the wings they are on retract so the boosters are tight to the body. Triangular wings swing out of the middle fuselage. In flight mode, no weapons are visible. In hover mode, weapons appear: two weapon pods extrude out, mounted on the diagonals of the fuselage, one on either side, both behind the canopy. In front of the canopy, two round ports open, and weapons slide out, just like the Polar Bear. The locked piece sits on top of the nose, flipped up like a hidden headlight on a sports car. That means 4 hardpoints and one locked.” The pods on the upper diagonals and the fourth mount a second Laser Carbine, his picks the same day. A first cut: it stands and fights in hover mode, the guns run out of the two round ports in the step behind the needle and the pods out of the chamfers behind the canopy, the Designator a pop-up on the nose's hood, up, its lens lit; on the map it changes into flight mode as it gathers speed (the weapons in and the ports' irises shut, the pop-up folded flush, the boosters swivelling level as the canards and tailplanes run in, the deltas swinging out) and back as it slows. Its acts: the transition (the change on the spot, a surge forward as a jet, and back), a sidestep, designating (the pop-up turning onto a mark and tipping down onto it), backpedalling on its boosters tipped back. Ryan's to judge running: the hangar's Walk for the change by speed, Acts for the transition.

giant_petrel.when: The catamaran, Ryan's mix of 12 November.
giant_petrel.note: Ryan, 31 October, of the first cut: “try a scratch version, but not a traditional catamaran. Something more like a military catamaran”; the second round's sheet the Navy SES as reviewed, with Kestrel's flair, and the racer. Ryan, 12 November: “The engines and rear spoiler of the racer, on the command ship body of the Navy SES take”, the SES as reviewed for its topside, his pick the same day. The SES's body whole: two knife hulls with raked stems, the cushion and its seals, the raised centre bow and its gun house, the full-beam deckhouse leaning in with the bridge's glass a band across its raked face, the upright faceted mast carrying the Reheat Uplink's array, the Spindrift Salvo's box flush in the roof behind it. The racer's stern: two giant boosters (the Immelmann Booster) between the hulls rising out of the deckhouse's aft end, and the swept cobalt aerofoil on two canted fins standing on the hulls' sterns. The engines take the quarterdeck where the SES's aft gun house stood, and the refit pass's placeholder in the vent's old slot makes a third gun, so the two Twin Autoguns ride the hulls' foredecks, a gun house on each (Claude's placement, his to move). Its acts: the salvo (the box's face rising out of the roof, its pairs firing), the Immelmann (the boosters burning, the hull lifting on the blast), the uplink, a traverse of the three gun houses together. A first cut, Ryan's to judge running.

lammergeier.when: First model, the flying wing, the launcher nacelles on the skin, 28 October.
lammergeier.note: The chrome chevron drawn as a hovercraft for the Giant Petrel (the third round, docs/looks/kestrel_giant.png), given to the Lammergeier airborne on Ryan's thought of 27 October ("looks good but careful on the weapon mount placement so they don't clip"): a deeper centre body with the canopy forward and the bomb bay under it on a lit seam, four booster drums across the trailing edge, the Syrinx Drone's tubes in the leading edge's roots, the Lorentz Contractor's dish on a dorsal pylon, the mounts on the wing in the bays between the drums. The last picture is the lay_mines act. 28 October: the drone tubes sit in a pod on each leading-edge root, its face raked with the edge, so the wing's skin no longer shows inside them (Ryan's note). His second notes (the pods did not work as meant): each is now a nacelle on the leading-edge root that carries the wing's full thickness forward to a blunt raked face, top and bottom, the two tubes let into the face. His third (the box was fine; the hull-coloured tube ends clipping through its raked face were the mistake): each tube's mouth follows the face's rake, a touch proud of it, in the nacelle's dark. His fourth: the tubes bored twelve deep (an end cap is no tube). His fifth (the mouths read as end caps, not inset): each mouth is a hole cut through the face plate, the bore flush in it in the lighter plate so its far wall catches the light. His sixth (the open bores showed the wing's skin again, which the caps had hidden: the skin climbs over the bore's depth): the nacelle rides on the wing's upper skin, its underside following the skin's rise from the edge, the tubes above the skin the whole way. His seventh: the bores dark, not the hull's light plate. Since 31 October its stock Incendiary Shells wear a burn weapon's fire over their rack, glowing shells dim at rest and flaring as they fire.

whip_scorpion.note: The mirror's mast is a gun (Ryan, 11 November: "an actual gun. Pipes connecting it to the boiler, steampunk style. Mirror or mirrors as part of it because weird future nonsense tech. Like a steam powered mirrored laser railgun"): a railgun on a pedestal off the cab's back, steam mains up from the waist, a hooped tank on its breech, a collector mirror over it, three relay mirrors down its rails and a lens in its muzzle; slid back in its mount the same day ("so it overhangs the back of the mount ... give the front some space and make a little scorpion vibe"), the breech and the collector out over the boiler. A first cut, to judge running. The last picture is the ray firing.
